meta.title: Prelude in C Minor (Op. 28, No. 20 - Full Piece)

theory.summary: Complete 13-bar Chopin masterpiece in C Minor featuring solemn four-voice chords, Neapolitan/diminished color, and chromatic bass motion.
theory.pattern_tip: Use Chord Skeleton mode first to memorize the 4-bar harmonic arches: Bars 1-4 (ff), Bars 5-8 (p echo), Bars 9-13 (pp + final cadence).
theory.technique_tip: Voice the top pinky note slightly louder than the inner chord tones so the melody sings across every chord change.
theory.ballade_link: Direct training in Chopin's signature 4-note chord voicing, dotted-8th + 16th inflection, and dark minor-key harmonic drama.
theory.concept_title: Cantabile Soprano Voicing & Neapolitan / Chromatic Harmony
concept_paragraphs: Chopin's C-minor Prelude proves you don't need fast notes to study conservatory harmony: 13 slow bars trace a solemn progression filled with mode color—including the poignant Neapolitan chord Db (bII) in Bar 2 and secondary twists (C/E, D7, V7/V).
Technically, every four-note chord demands top-note soprano voicing: transfer gentle arm weight into your RH 5th/4th fingers so the top melody sings like a choir over cushioned inner harmonies.

form_map.role: Noble opening declaration (Cm -> Ab -> Db (bII) -> G7 -> Cm) settling via D7 onto G.
Hushed echo introducing descending chromatic inner lines and sudden C7/G warmth.
Whispered reprise tapering to a solemn two-bar authentic C-minor cadence.

practice_steps: 1. Spend your first session entirely in Chord Skeleton / Wait-for-Note absorbing the chord shapes.
2. Voice the pinky (top voice) clearly above the thumb and inner fingers on every beat.
3. Isolate Bar 2 (Ab -> Db -> G7 -> Cm) and Bar 3 to hear the Neapolitan Db color cleanly.
4. Perform slowly at 56 BPM with deep, unforced resonance and crisp chord releases.
